description:
FILED AND SHIPPED s473p (Opus, 2026-09-07) as commit `688a7ab4`.

Round 27 named this lever and left it (plan-speed-and-ir-s470 §A.4.3, "AND ONE
LEVER THE SCALING CONTROL HANDED OVER FOR FREE"): with #1184's multi-array run
in, `feread2` read 0.28x of perl and `feread3` 0.30x while the SINGLE-array
`feread` still read 0.47x — a two-array loop was FASTER than a one-array loop
over the same 1000 elements.

THE CAUSE.  #1184's licence required TWO arrays because the flattening it
removed only exists for a multi-element list: `%p-flatten-for-list` hands a
lone bare lexical `@a` straight back, so there was nothing to save.  What it
hands back is the LIVE adjustable vector, and that IS the cost — every element
access is a hairy data-vector-ref and the bound is re-read per iteration —
while the run indexes each source's element-storage SIMPLE vector with `svref`
against a total snapshotted at loop entry.

THE FIX is `>= 2` becoming `>= 1` in `Pl::Parser::_foreach_bare_arrays`, and
nothing else: same emission, same runtime helpers, same registry name
(`foreach-arrays` — one transform with one fewer element in its shape test,
rule 11).

THE ONE SEMANTIC DIFFERENCE IS THE RE-READ BOUND, and the licence already
covers it.  `for (@a) { push @a, … }` iterates the new elements — probed perl
5.40.3 and PCL's live path both — and the run's snapshot would not.  But
push/pop/shift/unshift/splice/`$#a =`/a whole assignment inside the body are
all `written_in` for the #1140 array facts, and `escapes` covers every path a
callee or a closure could take to a `my` array, so the conjunct the caller
already applies declines exactly those loops.  Probed shape by shape: eight
write/escape shapes decline to the boxed `p-foreach`, nine licensed loops take
the run, and the lone SLICE and lone DEREF stay read-only-but-not-bare.

MEASURED (tools/bench-exec.pl, BENCH_K=5, quiet box, branch and base
alternating, two rounds):
    feread   0.1938 -> 0.1230 s   0.47x -> 0.30x   -36.5 %
    feread   0.1928 -> 0.1234 s   0.47x -> 0.30x   -36.0 %
CONTROLS in the same windows: intloop+= 0.0208/0.0208, intloop= 0.0187/0.0184,
cfor 0.0279/0.0275, arrfill 0.0285/0.0279, feread2 0.1285/0.1276, feread3
0.1210/0.1198, arrhash 0.0819/0.0817, arrhash-k 0.0603/0.0614, slices
0.1391/0.1326, listcopy 0.2227/0.2188, pushloc 0.0274/0.0288.
The plan asked for 0.47x -> ~0.28x; 0.30x is feread2's and feread3's own
reading, i.e. the array COUNT now costs nothing at one either.

BARS: gate 218 files / 7569 rows (13 pclxs xs rows only); corpus-diff 1 of 111
(split.t), silent drops 5 unchanged; emission A/B over 1007 files (25 lib + 402
cpan-tests + 580 of perl's own t/) SAME 966 / DIFF 41 / RCDIFF 0, with all 41
re-transpiled against a b5e9f845 extraction and classified — every one is the
same family; full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL 18674 (+0), drops 5 = census;
companion --jobs 1 over op/for.t op/array.t op/hash.t op/push.t op/eval.t
op/sort.t op/each.t, every file EQUAL to its baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv row,
ROW DIFF 0/0/0/0; ir-conform 289/0/56/0; ir-host-leak's symbol set identical to
b5e9f845's; `PCL_OPT=none` byte-identical to main's over 111 + 6.  Generation
v2-990, three artifacts regenerated (only the gen stamp moves).

GUARD Pl/t/perf-levers-01.t 54 -> 66 rows, inverse-verified (rows 53-55 fail on
b5e9f845).  THREE GUARDS WERE STALE against this change and were repaired in
the same commit (the s416 rule): foreach-raw-01.t rows 1+4, array-facts-01.t
rows 48+52, passes-01.t row 5 all asserted `(p-foreach-raw ($x @a))`, the
pre-#1409 spelling of a shape none of them is about; each now names the whole
CURRENT form, which is stronger than loosening the pattern.
subject: foreach-arrays: ONE bare array is a run too (#1184's licence needed two only because a one-element list has no flattening to remove)
